content.howTitle: How to compare two JSON files

steps.title: Paste or open the original JSON
steps.text: Put the first JSON document in the Original JSON box. You can paste it, or open or drag and drop a .json file.

steps.title: Add the changed JSON
steps.text: Put the second document in the Changed JSON box. Both are checked for errors and compared as you type.

steps.title: Review the changes
steps.text: See a list of every changed, added and removed value by its path, plus a side-by-side diff of both documents with their keys sorted.

content.featuresTitle: A JSON diff that understands JSON

features.title: Key order doesn't matter
features.text: Objects are compared by their keys, so the same data in a different order counts as equal.

features.title: Every change by path
features.text: Each difference is listed with its exact location, such as $.user.roles[2], and the old and new value.

features.title: Ignore array order
features.text: Turn it on when arrays are sets, like tags or IDs, and only additions and removals matter.

features.title: Finds invalid JSON
features.text: If a document can't be parsed, you see the line and column of the error, and Format tidies valid JSON.

features.title: Handles large files
features.text: Compares JSON files with 100,000+ lines in a background thread, so the page stays responsive.

features.title: 100% private
features.text: Nothing is uploaded. API responses, configs and data never leave your device.

uses.title: API responses
uses.text: Compare the response of two API versions or environments to find a changed field or a missing value.

uses.title: Configuration files
uses.text: Find the difference between two package.json, tsconfig, appsettings or other JSON config files.

uses.title: Test fixtures and snapshots
uses.text: See exactly why an expected and an actual JSON result don't match.

uses.title: Data exports
uses.text: Compare two exports of the same records to find what was added, removed or edited.

Paths such as $.settings.theme start at the document root $; [2] is the third item of an array.

faq.q: How do I compare two JSON files online?
faq.a: Paste the original JSON into the left box and the changed JSON into the right box, or open the files. DiffDuo lists every changed, added and removed value by its path and shows a side-by-side diff of both documents.

faq.q: Does the order of keys matter?
faq.a: No. Objects are compared by their keys, so two documents with the same data in a different key order are treated as equal. Formatting and whitespace are ignored too.

faq.q: Can I ignore the order of items in arrays?
faq.a: Yes. Turn on Ignore array order to compare arrays as sets. Items that appear in both arrays match wherever they are, and only added or removed items are reported.

faq.q: What does a path like $.user.roles[2] mean?
faq.a: It is the location of the value inside the document: $ is the root, .user is the user key, .roles is its roles key and [2] is the third item of that array.

faq.q: What happens if my JSON is invalid?
faq.a: DiffDuo shows which document has the error and the line and column where it is, so you can fix it. The Format button indents valid JSON to make it easier to read.

faq.q: Is my JSON uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. Everything runs in your browser, so your JSON never leaves your device. It is safe for API keys, customer data and internal configuration.

faq.q: Can it compare large JSON files?
faq.a: Yes. JSON files up to 50 MB can be opened, and the side-by-side diff runs in a background thread so the page stays responsive.

content.footer: DiffDuo: free online JSON compare and JSON diff tool. Everything runs locally, so your data never leaves the browser.
